title: How Ingredion Proved ROI at One Plant, Then Scaled
summary: How Ingredion proved ROI at one plant with condition monitoring: $1.0M in production savings, $223K in maintenance savings and a rollout across sites.
body_markdown:
## Key Points


- At North Kansas City, one pump failure with no spare meant a three-day shutdown.
- Continuous[vibration monitoring](https://tractian.com/en/glossary/vibration-monitoring) with AI diagnostics flagged looseness on a DSM pump with no backup before it forced a costly shutdown.
- One facility saved over $1M: $1.0M in production and $223K in maintenance.


Plant leaders who take a reliability case to finance usually get one last question before approval: has another plant already done this?


[Ingredion](https://tractian.com/en/case-studies/ingredion) has. Real-time condition monitoring helped it save over $1M in one facility, and the company is now scaling Tractian across its footprint.


## What was the problem costing the plant?


A critical pump with no spare parts failed at Ingredion's North Kansas City plant, and the plant went into a full three-day shutdown. Ingredion runs hundreds of machines around the clock across multiple facilities, and behind that failure the maintenance team faced problems traditional tools couldn't solve:


- **Hard-to-reach assets** slowed down inspections.
- **No early warnings:** with the methods they had, failures were often caught too late.
- **PMs missed subtle issues,** like alignment problems and bearing wear, that don't show up on a routine check until they're already serious.
- **Production losses added up fast** whenever equipment went down.


That's the kind of event your problem statement should be built on. If you haven't written yours yet, start with[how to define and quantify the problem before you ask for budget](https://tractian.com/en/blog/maintenance-budget-define-the-problem-before-you-ask) . A single failure on a[critical asset](https://tractian.com/en/glossary/critical-assets) , with its hours down and its cost, is usually more convincing to finance than a long list of maintenance pain points.


## What did continuous monitoring catch?


Ingredion partnered with Tractian to roll out real-time[condition monitoring](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/condition-monitoring) at key plants.


Vibration sensors and AI diagnostics now give the teams early alerts on issues like unbalance, looseness and lubrication problems, before they turn into full failures.


The clearest example was a DSM pump that had no backup and a known history of 3-day outages. The system detected a looseness defect on it, a work order was issued immediately, and a costly shutdown was avoided.


The cost of the alternative was already known from the pump's own outage history, which made the catch easy to value.


Not every finding was that dramatic. Some were issues the team says it would not have noticed without Tractian. Jacob Hoffine, Reliability Engineer, described one of them:


*"There were some issues that I would say, if not for having Tractian, we would have never noticed… For example, a lubrication problem, we could go out and lubricate it and recheck it on Tractian platform and see that it fixed the problem… It was pretty impressive for that, the results we got early on."*


A fix confirmed on the platform gives finance a closed finding it can count.


## What did it deliver in numbers?


In one facility alone, Ingredion recorded $1.0M in production savings and $223K in maintenance savings, with up to 168 hours of downtime avoided across critical equipment.


Result One facility


Production savings $1.0M


Maintenance savings $223K


Total Over $1M at one plant


Downtime avoided Up to 168 hours across critical equipment


Standout finding Looseness defect on a DSM pump with no backup and a history of 3-day outages


Production and maintenance savings sit on separate lines for a reason. Production value (the output you didn't lose) and maintenance value (the repairs, parts and labor you didn't spend) are checked by different people, using different numbers, so finance can verify each on its own instead of questioning a single blended total. Learn more about[how to build a predictive maintenance business case](https://tractian.com/en/blog/predictive-maintenance-business-case-how-to-build-one) .


The downtime figure is a range: Ingredion reports 48 to 168 hours of avoided downtime, and up to 168 hours is the top of it. If you're presenting your own results, do the same: show the range and say which end you're relying on.


## How did one plant's result turn into a decision to scale?


The facility delivered clear, tangible ROI from condition-based alerts and faster issue resolution, and with successful implementations at multiple sites Ingredion is scaling Tractian solutions across its footprint. A result at one plant, stated in money, with production and maintenance value on separate lines and a clear finding behind it, gives leadership a reason to fund the next site.


If you're planning your own pilot, that result is the standard to build toward.


A one-page day-90 report to finance can make the same case with confirmed findings, their validated value, cost to date and a projection to more sites. Learn more about[proving ROI in a 90-day pilot](https://tractian.com/en/blog/maintenance-metrics-that-prove-roi-in-a-90-day-pilot) .


## What changed for the team?


Before, the plant relied on inspections that were slowed by hard-to-reach assets and PMs that missed early signs of wear. Now the team gets alerts with clear, guided recommendations, takes corrective action with confidence and spends less time on manual inspections. Maintenance resources go where the data says they're needed.


Rafael Padilha, Maintenance & Reliability Director, US/CAN, described the shift:


*"Reliability roles are evolving. We're becoming data scientists, not just wrench turners."*


That matters in a budget meeting where monitoring can sound like a headcount cut. In the same quote, Padilha says the team is "not heading toward job loss."


## FAQ


**How much did Ingredion save with condition monitoring?** At a single Ingredion facility, savings reached $1.0M on the production side and $223K on maintenance, with between 48 and 168 hours of downtime avoided on critical equipment.


**What did the monitoring system catch at Ingredion?** Vibration sensors and AI diagnostics flagged unbalance, looseness and lubrication problems. The standout was looseness on the DSM pump, an asset with no backup, found in time to issue a work order and avoid a costly shutdown.


**Is Ingredion using condition monitoring at more than one plant?** Yes. Ingredion has successful implementations at multiple sites and is rolling Tractian out further.


## How can your plant follow the same path?


Start with one facility and the critical assets whose failures you can already price, prove the return there, then take that result to leadership as the case for more sites.


[Schedule a meeting](https://tractian.com/en/contact) with Tractian to plan your pilot and the case that comes after it. Tractian sensors are[Class I Div 1 ATEX/IECEx/NFPA compliant](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/sensor-specifications) and can be installed in a single day without cabling or an IT project. Tractian's focus is condition monitoring, and it[connects with popular CMMS platforms](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/integrations) (MaintainX, Fiix, UpKeep, Limble) and ERPs (SAP, Oracle NetSuite).
